terra.problem: The passage does not specify cows, sheep, coins, or bars of gold.
Moving his tent does not establish that Abram had no deed or land.
Abram's earlier worship at this spot is outside the passage and needs a reference, such as Genesis 12:8.
The kitchen-keys joke compares the altar to an ordinary object and makes its holiness part of the joke.
The land's inability to support them is reduced to a crowded, tight squeeze. The text does not say physical space was the problem.
The cookie comparison does not clearly work: one rack's worth of cookies might fit on one tray, and the two people do not make the shortage clear.
Lot being Abram's nephew needs a reference outside the passage. The workers bumping into each other all day and having attitude are also invented.
Identifying Pharaoh as Egypt's king is a fact from outside the passage and needs a reference.
The text does not say the dispute was over where cows grazed.
Abram offers to go the other way, but the passage does not say he actually traveled in the opposite direction after Lot chose.
The text does not say the water is what made the plain look good to Lot.
The explanation is generic and repeats that trees are not mentioned without adding much personality.
This simply repeats Lot's choice and departure without much of Papa Dorin's voice.
His earlier worship at the altar needs an outside reference, such as Genesis 12:8. The passage also does not establish that Abram turns to the LORD everywhere he settles.
The earlier altar was between Bethel and Ai, not stated to be at Bethel. The text also does not say worship was Abram's first action at Hebron.
